title: Measure which standards injections change a diff and stop repeating served records
body:
Lead observation 2026-11-17: PreToolUse standards packets were injected on most Bash calls, mostly the same generic TypeScript records (no-any, no-suppressions, no-star-reexport, deep-relative-imports), and changed no decision in the session's diffs; the useful catches came from guard tests (receivers.json, boundaries, README command table). Self-report only, not a measurement.
Outcome: `krn ledger --standards-effect` prints one line with the share (0-1) of standards injections followed by a diff touching the record subject over the last 20 sessions and the repeat count per session; when the share is below 0.2, a record already served in the session is not injected again (exit 0, a test asserts the second injection is absent).
Proof: a ledger/standards command prints the share of injections followed by a diff touching the record's subject over the last N sessions, and the repeat count per session.
